contexts.text: They placed Helicon on a mountain, and by it they meant Heaven.
The maidens whom they called the Heliconides and Parnassides were the affections of truth.
[151a]. The higher hill is called the Heliconeum. CL 182.
I saw a certain one upon the Heliconeum with a trumpet...
Diogenes with his scholars stays beneath the Heliconeum...
It was from this that the Gentiles in Greece placed Helicon on a high mountain...
For a mountain, thus Helicon, from correspondence = the higher Heaven...
